string-array.item: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship (AUS) is a merit-based financial award funded by Singaporean universities (such as NUS, NTU, SMU, and SIT) to support outstanding high school graduates from ASEAN member countries (excluding Singapore) pursuing full-time undergraduate degrees. \n Recipients generally receive coverage for tuition fees as well as a living allowance, allowing high-achieving students across the region to access world-class education without financial barriers.

The University of British Columbia (UBC) International Scholarships is a financial awards offered to incoming international students, broadly categorized into merit-based entrance awards and need-plus-merit awards \n As a Scholar, you’ll get to participate in skill building workshops and retreats and have the option to participate in exchange and co-op. While you work on your degree, you’ll have additional support from dedicated International Scholars Program advisors who will encourage your academic, personal and career development.

The UNIST International Student Scholarship is a merit-based financial award provided by the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST)—one of South Koreas premier science and technology research universities. Like other top Korean STEM institutes, UNIST offers comprehensive scholarship support to almost all admitted international undergraduate students.\n This financial aid usually includes full tuition exemption along with a monthly living stipend, helping students focus fully on their cutting-edge scientific and engineering studies.

Study in Saudi is a fully funded government program administered by the Saudi Ministry of Education to attract top international talent to public universities across the Kingdom\n The scholarship offers comprehensive coverage, including full tuition waiver, subsidized housing, medical care, and round-trip airfare tickets for selected candidates.

Beasiswa Garuda (specifically Beasiswa Garuda Sarjana) is a prestigious, fully funded undergraduate scholarship program created through a collaboration between the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Technology (Kemdiktisaintek) and the Education Fund Management Institution (LPDP).\n It aims to nurture exceptional Indonesian talent by providing full support for tuition, living expenses, book allowances, and insurance during their academic journey.

USC awards scholarships to help undergraduate students pay for their education. These funds come from a variety of university, federal, state and private sources. Unlike loans, however, they do not have to be repaid.\n Most USC merit scholarships are awarded during the admission review process, considering a student’s academic performance, leadership skills, and community involvement.

CUHK offers admission scholarships to both local and non-local new undergraduate students on the basis of their excellent academic or non-academic performance. There is no need for the students to apply for these scholarships. The University will identify qualified new students and inform the selected students of the scholarship offers.\n These awards serve to attract high-caliber students globally, offering renewable tuition coverage or cash grants based on ongoing academic achievements.

The KAIST International Student Undergraduate Scholarship is a fully funded merit award offered by the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)—one of Asias top STEM universities. Nearly all admitted international undergraduate students automatically receive this scholarship upon admission.\n In addition to full tuition coverage for eight semesters, scholars are provided with a national health insurance allowance and monthly living stipends, provided they maintain academic standards.

The Nagoya University Global 30 (G30) Undergraduate Scholarship is a merit- and need-based financial award for outstanding international students enrolling in English-taught undergraduate degree programs at Nagoya University, Japan.\n Designed to lower barriers for global talent, the award covers tuition fees and grants a monthly stipend to support living expenses throughout the degree program.

The King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM) SAT Track is a fully funded undergraduate admission and scholarship pathway for local and international students.\n Through this streamlined application channel based on SAT scores, high-performing students gain access to full tuition, free textbooks, campus housing, and monthly living allowances.
